title: Add feature flag for staged provision-to-ready rollout (region + pool type) with kill switch
author: Jordan Lee
description: Context: As part of the provision-to-ready automation sprint we need to enable the new orchestration + validation flow gradually (starting with us-east / A100 / Dedicated) and retain a fast rollback path if failure rates spike. This PR introduces a control-plane feature flag that gates whether the staged provisioning flow is enabled for a given node based on (region, pool type), with a global kill switch that forces legacy provisioning behavior. Summary of changes: (1) Adds a ProvisioningRolloutPolicy evaluator in the control plane that decides between LegacyProvisioning and StagedProvisioning for each node join event. The evaluator checks a global kill switch first, then a scoped allowlist keyed by region and pool_type (dedicated/shared), and finally defaults to legacy. (2) Adds admin-only APIs to update rollout policy (set allowlist entries, toggle kill switch) and read-only endpoints for internal tooling to query the current effective policy and last-updated metadata. (3) Emits audit logs + structured events when rollout policy changes (who/when/what), and includes the policy decision (legacy vs staged) as a tag in readiness transition events (without including per-node identifiers). (4) Adds docs for operators: how to enable staged provisioning by region, how to disable via kill switch, and how to verify via metrics and readiness service state. Behavior details: Global kill switch (provisioning.rollout.kill_switch=true) forces legacy provisioning for all regions/pools and suppresses any allowlist entries. Scoped rollout allowlist supports exact matches on region and pool_type; pool_type is taken from fleet metadata (dedicated/shared) and validated at the boundary. If metadata is missing/invalid we default to legacy and emit a warning event (no hard failure). Rollout changes take effect immediately for new nodes entering Allocated->Provisioning; we do not attempt to migrate nodes already in Validating mid-flight. Tests included: unit tests for policy precedence and default behavior; API authz tests (admin vs read-only); integration-style test that simulates a node join and asserts the provisioner selection. Rollout plan: Land behind the default-off policy. Infra will enable allowlist for us-east + dedicated only during the staged rollout window (ENG-4829) with SRE on-call coverage. Kill switch can be toggled by on-call with the existing break-glass admin role. Links: ADR-017 readiness state machine (policy decision is recorded as part of the provisioning step metadata), ENG-4822 control-plane state machine implementation, SUP-28411 customer report motivating faster rollback mechanisms.
commits: Add rollout policy evaluator and kill switch precedence
Expose admin and internal read-only APIs for rollout policy
Emit audit events for rollout policy changes; tag provisioning decision in events
Add rolloutctl helper and operator documentation
Tests: authz + policy evaluation + node join integration
review_conversation: Ethan Park: Can we make sure the kill switch is evaluated before any allowlist lookup? I want to be confident that flipping one flag is enough during an incident.
Jordan Lee (author): Yep — policy evaluation order is now: kill_switch -> allowlist match -> default legacy. Added a unit test that asserts allowlist entries are ignored when kill_switch=true.
Rafael Mendes: Please confirm we are not tagging per-node IDs in metrics/events. We just got bitten by high-cardinality tags last quarter.

Jordan Lee (author): Confirmed. The readiness/provisioning decision is included as a low-cardinality enum (legacy|staged) plus region + pool_type. No node_id tags; audit event includes actor + policy key only.
Vanessa Ortiz: How do we treat missing pool_type? Some older pools don’t have the tag in fleet metadata yet.
Jordan Lee (author): Missing/unknown pool_type falls back to legacy with a warning event (rate-limited). We can tighten this once Terraform tags are fully rolled out.
Connor O'Brien: Docs look good. Can you add one explicit 'rollback' section with the exact command and expected verification steps?
Jordan Lee (author): Added a rollback section to docs/internal/fleet/provision-to-ready/rollout-flags.md including rolloutctl examples and which dashboard panels to check.
Keiko Yamamoto: Minor naming nit: please align pool_type values with what autoscaling uses (dedicated/shared).
Jordan Lee (author): Updated constants and API validation to use dedicated/shared, added backwards-compatible parsing for 'on_demand' in case we see it from older tags.
release_notes: Internal-only: Adds rollout gating for staged provision-to-ready automation by region and pool type, including a global kill switch and operator docs. Default remains legacy until allowlist is enabled during staged rollout.
